Will you colonize nearby planets or take them by force? Produce resources for trade and research new technologies to build the best empire and win the game! Eminent Domain is an empire building game in which your empire’s abilities are based on a deck of Role cards. Every turn you must choose a role to execute and in doing so you will add one of those Role cards to your deck. When executing a role, you may Boost its effect by playing cards out of your hand matching the role you have chosen. For example, the more research done by your empire, the better your empire gets at doing research - because there will be more research cards in your deck! Planets typically score between two (2) and five (5) influence a piece. Goods (and sometimes fighters) score typically one influence a piece and are renewable. Researched technologies scores two (2) or five (5) for intermediate and advanced cards. Gameplay At the start of the game and the end of your turn, you are dealt a hand of cards from your deck. You customize your deck as you go. During other player's turn you may either Follow their role and perform the actions using cards in your hand or Dissent giving you an additional card to use later. On your turn you may perform an Action and must perform a Role . If at any time you get the message you have yet to do something, you probably have a passive ability that you may use at the time. Review your cards in front of you to ensure you are getting the most of your turn Action phase On your turn, you may first take an Action . This is done by selecting a single card from your hand. Only the Action listed on the card is performed and other players may not follow. Role phase After your action, you then take a Role . You may always select any role, and this will usually give you a card from the relevant role stack which will be added to your deck. When you play a role, its strength can be further boosted by also playing cards from your hand with the matching symbol. Once this is done, every other player may either follow your role or dissent in which case they are dealt one card from their deck into their hand. Cleanup phase After you have played a role, you must discard your hand down to your current card limit (starts at 5, may increase) or less. Additional cards you will discard have an outline on them. You will then draw new cards from your deck up to your card limit. Dissent/Follow phase - Inactive player(s) During other players' turns you are given the ability to follow the Role of the current player. This allows you to perform an additional albeit limited version of the Role phase . If you choose to Dissent instead you draw an additional card from your deck to your hand. Game end The game ends in the round that follows the depletion of a number of role card stacks (1 stack for 2-3 player game, 2 stacks for 4-5 player game), or when the influence token supply is exhausted. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] This game combines the worst of Dominion and Race for the Galaxy in my opinion.  I dislike both of them and dislike this one even more.  UGH and MEH - I cannot say enough against it.  Nothing new and not worthy of my time.  I would not even play it to be polite or if there was not another choice.

[Rating: 1/10] Almost the worst deck building game.  It is slightly different, but feels very fidgety, and its one of those games that always makes you feel like your losing, even when your doing well.  It clearly lacks replayability, since the games vary so little from game to game, mostly due to the lack of stressers that would encourage a player to take one route or another.  You only get to make one of five actions, but realistically 4, since colonization and warfare conflict with each other, and its at least slightly detrimental to try doing both.

[Rating: 1/10] Less than average deckbuilder, up there with Nightfall.  One victory path, meh production, the WORST run Kickstarter campaign to date, and as a bonus it's rated a 10 by the designer and publisher, who are the types to gripe about manufactured ratings, and in Seth's case be extremely critical of well designed games.  Do yourself a favor and don't bother.

[Rating: 1/10] This game is bad and completely broken in my opinion.  If everyone picks the same action repeatedly and runs one of the action decks out, the game is over before it even starts.  When people asked about this on the forums, the designer told people they were playing wrong.  What a joke.

[Rating: 1/10] Race for the galaxy is so much better than this game.  I think this game is about a 3-4, but I dropped rating to a 1 to offset designers rating of 10.  Dont bother with this one!

[Rating: 1/10] This game is like Race For The Galaxy except it's not any fun.  I played it twice and both times were awful.  Just play Race instead.

[Rating: 1/10] ....very professional publisher... rated 10 all of his games (nothing bad here...) and rated 1 to 3 most of te best game around.... ....uhm....yes very professional. ;)

[Rating: 1/10] [u]First impression:[/u] San Juan meets deck building while trying to look like RFTG. Some clever things like adding cards to the deck being mandatory and at the same time being used as a timing mechanism. While it is much, much simpler to grasp than RFTG, maybe even San Juan - as everything is done with copies of 5 basic card and the unique cards are used sparingly - it has the same problem as Dominion for me. The logic of playing well is to wrap your head around the system which doesn't exactly hint at how does it want to be used and I guess there is space to explore there, but I don't care 

[Rating: 1/10] Felt like it needed a few more passes of development/ editing, didn't quite hang together as a game. Disappointing when the inspiring games, Race for the Galaxy, Dominion and Glory to Rome are all amazing and super tightly playing games.

[Rating: 1/10] a mix between Race for the Galaxy and Dominion, and it is worse than both of them

[Rating: 2/10] Yeay, another Dominion. At least it is not the clustermess called Thunderstone  The microcosm version simply obsoleted this game for me.

[Rating: 2/10] This game has flaws, that I hope will be worked out with an expansion.  Action vs. role is not always intuative, and I messed this up sometimes in my head, though playing correctly. Playing with 3 players, we found that the standard version of the game would be over before it even began. Colonize cards were gone almost at the start of the game. We decided to play the extended version only to have the same happen almost as fast to the research deck.  I hope this game will be fixed, because I see great potential, but as is it is shelved in my collection for now.

[Rating: 2/10] An under-designed and especially under-developed hybrid of Dominion and Race for the Galaxy, which fails to capture the magic of either of those titles.  I'm not sure the core of the game can ever become part of a satisfying game: fundamentally it becomes extremely difficult to manage your deck when each time you take a role you have to add another card for it to your deck. [Rating: 2/10] This one was really bad, I can't see how it's ranked as high as it is. If you wan't deck-building this is not the game you want cause you have no real control of your deck. And you don't have any time to build a deck of combos either. The game end is too easy to achieve for a rushing player which makes the settling-strategy too simple and too effective. Very boring game I though.

[Rating: 2/10] Extremely generic and uninteresting deck-building game. Seems to follow in the steps of Race for the Galaxy, another game I dislike.

[Rating: 2/10] Quite ok but there are much better deck builders.  Update 2016: Reduced down to 2. Never again.
